reviews.title: Sleeping Beauty
reviews.verdictRationale: Aurora's caretakers and Prince Phillip show affection, steadfastness and courage in opposing Maleficent. Yet Aurora has little agency, the curse drives the plot, and romance is tied to an enchanted sleep. Fairy-tale magic is openly fictional but central to the story; parents can praise loyalty without presenting an unconscious heroine's rescue as a general model of relationships.
reviews.ageRationale: Maleficent’s minions, abduction, hypnotic curse and dragon battle can be scary for young children. The kiss of a sleeping person also warrants conversation about consent and storytelling conventions.
reviews.synopsis: An infant princess is cursed by a jealous fairy and sheltered until a prince faces a dragon to break the spell.

themes.name: Loyal care and protection
themes.evidence: The good fairies sacrifice comfort to guard Aurora from Maleficent.

themes.name: Courage against intimidation
themes.evidence: Phillip faces the dangerous dragon to rescue Aurora.

themes.name: Coercion through a curse
themes.evidence: Maleficent uses magic to threaten and immobilize a young woman.

themes.name: Passive romance convention
themes.evidence: Aurora’s rescue depends on others and a kiss during enchanted unconsciousness.

reviews.reflection: Why do the fairies try so hard to guard Aurora? Talk about the difference between loving protection and controlling another person’s choices.
questions: What moves the fairies to protect Aurora?
Why is Maleficent angry at a child who has done nothing to her?
Which part of the rescue involves actual courage?
Would someone’s unconsciousness matter when discussing consent in real life?
What would a version of this story give Aurora more freedom to choose?

themeScripture.connection: Discuss patience and protection within love without treating the fairy tale as a moral rulebook.

reviews.title: Alice in Wonderland
reviews.verdictRationale: Alice's curiosity carries her into a world whose characters are often rude, unpredictable or openly cruel. The story resists intimidation—especially the Queen's threats—without offering a sustained lesson about spiritual growth. It is principally an imaginative, absurdist adventure. Families can discuss self-control and the difference between nonsense and truth, alongside the persistent smoking imagery.
reviews.ageRationale: A threatening queen, near-drowning, confusing transformations and the Caterpillar’s hookah may worry or bewilder young viewers. Seven and older leaves room to separate surreal fantasy from appropriate behavior.
reviews.synopsis: A curious girl tumbles through Wonderland, meeting strange creatures and a queen obsessed with punishment.

themes.name: Curiosity and perseverance
themes.evidence: Alice keeps seeking her way through a confusing world.

themes.name: Resistance to cruel power
themes.evidence: Alice eventually resists the Queen’s threats and accusations.

themes.name: Threats and arbitrary punishment
themes.evidence: The Queen repeatedly calls for executions in a comic but menacing world.

themes.name: Hookah smoking and irrationality
themes.evidence: The Caterpillar frequently smokes while other characters model foolish or discourteous behavior.

reviews.reflection: Alice hears one unreasonable rule after another. Ask when a child should respectfully challenge what an authority figure says.
questions: Which characters give Alice a reason to trust them?
Why is the Queen’s idea of justice unfair?
What do the repeated size changes make Alice feel?
How should we respond if someone tries to make harmful behavior look sophisticated?
What is the difference between asking questions and simply arguing?

themeScripture.connection: Consider the importance of listening and understanding before accepting a claim.

reviews.title: The Rescuers
reviews.verdictRationale: Bernard and Bianca travel far to protect Penny, whose vulnerability is exploited by an adult who values a jewel above a child. The film makes courage, compassion and persistence admirable, while treating abduction and manipulation as wrong. The frightening situations are unusually intense for a gentle-looking animated movie, so the age recommendation is higher than the title might suggest.
reviews.ageRationale: Kidnapping, the threat of drowning, crocodiles and gunfire put a child in repeated peril. Ten and older is an independent conservative suggestion for sensitive viewers.
reviews.synopsis: Two brave mice travel to rescue an orphaned girl from an exploitative adult in a swamp hideout.

themes.name: Protection of the vulnerable
themes.evidence: Bernard and Bianca take a risk to help a girl whose captor has more power.

themes.name: Courage and partnership
themes.evidence: The rescuers cooperate despite their differences and fears.

themes.name: Child exploitation
themes.evidence: Madame Medusa manipulates and endangers Penny for a treasure.

themes.name: Sustained child peril
themes.evidence: Water danger, crocodiles and threatening weapons recur.

reviews.reflection: Penny has little control over the people holding her captive. Discuss why protecting a child is worth inconvenience and danger to those able to help.
questions: Why is Penny unable to escape without help?
What makes Bernard and Bianca decide she is worth risking themselves for?
How does Medusa use promises to control someone smaller?
Why is bravery not the same as having no fear?
How can our family support someone vulnerable in our community?

themeScripture.connection: Explore speaking up for those who cannot defend themselves.

reviews.title: The Rescuers Down Under
reviews.verdictRationale: Cody refuses to abandon animals threatened by an adult hunter, and Bernard and Bianca again put another's welfare above their convenience. The film treats greed, captivity and cruelty as plainly wrong, though its action-adventure tone is a considerable part of the experience. Cooperation, protection and faithful friendship make the positive message more than decoration.
reviews.ageRationale: A boy is taken captive and faces crocodiles, animal abuse, falls and violent threats. Ten and older gives margin for children upset by endangered kids or animals.
reviews.synopsis: Rescue mice return to save an Australian boy and a rare eagle from a ruthless poacher.

themes.name: Mercy toward creatures
themes.evidence: Cody tries to free a rare eagle instead of letting the hunter harm it.

themes.name: Faithful cooperation
themes.evidence: The rescue partners persist in reaching a captive child.

themes.evidence: A poacher threatens a child and animals to obtain what he wants.

themes.name: Kidnapping and danger
themes.evidence: Cody faces armed captivity, crocodiles and near-fatal falls.

reviews.reflection: Cody chooses to protect a creature even when doing so becomes dangerous. How do we care wisely for those entrusted to us?
questions: Why does Cody keep the eagle’s location secret?
Which helpers are brave even when they are unsure what to do?
How does the poacher treat living creatures as possessions?
Are there safer ways for adults to protect animals in real life?

reviews.title: Hercules
reviews.verdictRationale: Hercules begins by wanting to be celebrated and accepted among the gods, but the story ultimately defines a hero by sacrificial love rather than fame or strength. Hades' ambition and manipulation are villainous, and Meg's choices reveal a more complicated struggle with trust. Disney's Greek gods and the underworld are a mythological fantasy, not Christian teaching about divinity, death or salvation. The core lesson about self-giving deserves praise with that distinction kept clear.
reviews.ageRationale: Monster fights, underworld images, a cigar-smoking villain and flirtatious jokes warrant some context. Ten and older permits comparison of mythology and Christian belief.
reviews.synopsis: An awkward young demigod trains to become a hero and confronts a ruler of the mythological underworld.

themes.name: Self-sacrificial love
themes.evidence: Hercules risks himself for Meg instead of seeking only public glory.

themes.name: Humility beyond fame
themes.evidence: The film contrasts the desire for applause with a costly act of love.

themes.name: Vanity and manipulation
themes.evidence: Hades and fame-driven choices expose the danger of self-serving ambition.

themes.name: Pagan deity and underworld imagery
themes.evidence: Greek gods, supernatural creatures and an imagined afterlife are central to the plot.

reviews.reflection: What makes Hercules heroic in the end: the crowds praising him or the choice to put another person first?
questions: Why does Hercules think becoming famous will make him belong?
What changes his understanding of a true hero?
Which promises does Hades make that are designed to deceive?
How is the film’s underworld different from Christian belief?
Can a person be courageous without being admired?

themeScripture.connection: Discuss sacrificial love as a virtue while keeping the movie's Greek mythology separate from the Gospel.

reviews.title: Tarzan
reviews.verdictRationale: Kala's adoption of Tarzan gives the film a strong picture of care that crosses biological boundaries. Tarzan must decide what loyalty, identity and family mean as the hunters' greed threatens those who sheltered him. Violence and exploitation are depicted as threats, not ideals. The romance is secondary to the story's defense of compassion and belonging.
reviews.ageRationale: A leopard attack, armed hunters, separation and an upsetting death may trouble younger viewers. Ten and older offers room to discuss loss and the danger of exploiting animals.
reviews.synopsis: A boy raised by gorillas struggles to understand his identity when humans arrive in the forest.

themes.name: Family love beyond biology
themes.evidence: Kala cares for Tarzan and the troop becomes his family.

themes.name: Protection of the vulnerable
themes.evidence: Tarzan defends those who sheltered him when exploitation threatens.

themes.name: Greed and exploitation
themes.evidence: The hunters treat animals and the forest as resources to dominate.

themes.name: Animal attacks and grief
themes.evidence: Predator attacks, weapons and a death create serious emotional stakes.

reviews.reflection: Who becomes a parent through steadfast care rather than shared appearance? Ask what the film says about belonging and responsibility.
questions: How does Kala show she is Tarzan’s mother?
Why does Tarzan feel divided after meeting Jane?
What does Clayton value more than living creatures?
How can loving animals avoid reckless risks in real life?
Does being different from our family make us any less loved?

themeScripture.connection: Use Paul's call to honor one another to discuss loyalty within an adoptive family.

reviews.title: Atlantis: The Lost Empire
reviews.verdictRationale: Milo's curiosity and concern for a threatened people move the film toward resisting exploitation, yet the expedition's greed and betrayal drive much of the action. The glowing crystal and Atlantean beliefs are portrayed as powerful, mysterious elements of an invented civilization; parents should not confuse them with Orthodox spirituality. Its best lesson is about protecting others rather than possessing everything we discover, but the overall experience is chiefly an action-fantasy adventure.
reviews.ageRationale: Combat, explosions, smoking, alcohol references and the ominous power of a mystical crystal support ten and older. Younger viewers may be unsettled by death and betrayal.
reviews.synopsis: A young linguist joins an expedition to a lost city and must choose between discovery and protecting its people.

themes.name: Respect for others and their home
themes.evidence: Milo comes to defend Atlantis rather than exploit its population.

themes.name: Courage against betrayal
themes.evidence: He resists expedition members who turn on the people they encounter.

themes.name: Colonial greed and exploitation
themes.evidence: The villains seek to seize powerful resources without regard for harm.

themes.name: Mysticism and armed peril
themes.evidence: The story includes a supernatural crystal, weapons, destruction and drinking.

reviews.reflection: When does exploration stop being learning and become taking what belongs to someone else?

reviews.title: Meet the Robinsons
reviews.verdictRationale: Lewis is afraid that rejection defines his worth and looks to an invented future to solve the pain of his past. His growing relationships show that being loved does not depend on erasing every mistake or recovering an imagined perfect family. The story admires resilience, forgiveness and chosen family, while its fantastical machines are science fiction rather than occult instructions.
reviews.ageRationale: Comic invention mishaps, a robotic hat menace, fear of abandonment and brief danger may unsettle very young children. Seven and older should allow conversation about adoption and belonging.
reviews.synopsis: An orphaned young inventor travels into a chaotic future and discovers the value of the people willing to welcome him.

themes.name: Belonging and welcome
themes.evidence: A family embraces Lewis as he is rather than demanding perfection.

themes.name: Persistence after mistakes
themes.evidence: Failed inventions become chances to learn, not reasons to give up.

themes.name: Resentment and sabotage
themes.evidence: The antagonist lets past grievance grow into a plan to harm others.

themes.name: Futuristic threats
themes.evidence: Robots, a dinosaur and dangerous inventions create comic peril.

reviews.reflection: Lewis fears that not knowing his birth mother means something is wrong with him. Discuss how people can offer family and welcome in the present.
questions: What does Lewis think he must learn about his past to belong?

What happens when a person clings to a childhood grievance?
How does the story redefine a failed experiment?
How can we make someone feel genuinely included in our family or community?

themeScripture.connection: Explore God's concern for those without secure family support without claiming the film teaches theology.

reviews.title: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York
reviews.verdictRationale: Kevin's conversations with a lonely woman and his desire to return to his family are genuinely warm. Still, the film repeatedly turns extreme physical retaliation into a source of laughter; the villains' wrongdoing does not make every dangerous trap an example worth copying. Because kindness and reconciliation coexist with spectacular slapstick, a Neutral assessment best preserves the distinction.
reviews.ageRationale: The traps, fires, falls and blunt-force impacts are exaggerated but highly imitable; mild language and a background adult-film sign also warrant care. Ten and older leaves more room to discuss real-world injury.

themes.evidence: Kevin wants to return home and repair strained relationships.

themes.evidence: Severe injuries from traps are treated as comic entertainment.

themes.name: Disrespectful speech and behavior
themes.evidence: Arguments and insulting language accompany Kevin’s efforts to navigate the city.

reviews.title: The Sandlot
reviews.verdictRationale: The boys form a lasting friendship through games, mistakes and a surprising act of neighborliness, and their courage in approaching an old neighbor challenges a false story about his dog. But the film also normalizes objectifying girls, rough insults and a nonconsensual kiss as part of its nostalgic comedy. A Neutral verdict credits belonging without excusing what the boys wrongly admire.
reviews.ageRationale: Profanity, chewing tobacco, bullying, a nonconsensual kiss played for laughs and gender stereotyping make this less suitable for younger children despite a friendly baseball setting. Thirteen and older is a cautious independent recommendation.
reviews.synopsis: A new boy finds friends through neighborhood baseball, where mischief and a feared dog complicate one summer.

themes.name: Friendship and belonging
themes.evidence: The team welcomes Scotty and includes him in their summer adventures.

themes.name: Courage to correct rumors
themes.evidence: The boys finally learn the truth about the feared dog and its owner.

themes.name: Objectification and nonconsensual kiss
themes.evidence: A lifeguard is treated as a prize, and a boy tricks her into a kiss.

themes.name: Profanity and tobacco imitation
themes.evidence: Boys use crude language and experiment with chewing tobacco before becoming sick.

reviews.reflection: Being included by friends can make a childhood memorable. But friendship should not require laughing at someone else's boundaries.

reviews.title: The Goonies
reviews.verdictRationale: The young adventurers refuse to give up on their community and learn to work together despite disagreements. That solidarity is appealing, but crude jokes, invasive looking, strong language and reckless risk-taking are frequent enough that family viewing needs substantial discernment. The film is more a rambunctious treasure adventure than a sustained encouragement to spiritual growth.
reviews.ageRationale: Strong profanity for its period, suggestive jokes, an upskirt-looking incident, frightening threats and violent criminals make the original PG rating misleading for some families. Thirteen and older is a cautious independent guide, not a promise of suitability.
reviews.synopsis: A group of friends searches for buried pirate treasure while trying to save their neighborhood from redevelopment.

themes.name: Loyalty and teamwork
themes.evidence: The children collaborate during dangerous passages to help each other and protect their homes.

themes.name: Courage against greed
themes.evidence: The group persists despite thieves, traps and a plan to displace their families.

themes.name: Profanity and sexualized jokes
themes.evidence: The children and teens use coarse dialogue and treat an upskirt intrusion as a gag.

themes.name: Violence and reckless danger
themes.evidence: Armed criminals, threatening traps and frightening falls recur.

reviews.reflection: The Goonies act to protect their homes, but some of their jokes hurt people. Discuss how shared courage should be matched by respect for others.
questions: Why do the friends begin the treasure hunt?
Which character feels excluded, and how does the group respond?
Which jokes disrespect another person’s dignity or privacy?
When does courage become an unnecessary risk?
If the group cared for the neighborhood, what other solutions might they have tried?

themeScripture.connection: Consider the difference between something being entertaining and something being beneficial to imitate.
